slides: Let's continue with work and rate, and look at the units first.

slides.say: A rate has a time unit, per minute or per hour. So before we calculate, the units must match.
One hour is sixty minutes. So from hours to minutes, we multiply by sixty.
Three hours is three times sixty, a hundred eighty minutes.
at: Three hours is three times sixty

slides.say: From minutes to hours, we divide by sixty. Thirty minutes is thirty over sixty, half an hour.
at: Thirty minutes is thirty over sixty

slides.say: And twenty minutes is twenty over sixty, a third of an hour.
at: twenty minutes is twenty over sixty

slides.say: Let's see why it matters. A machine makes four parts a minute. How many parts does it make in two hours?
at: A machine makes four parts a minute

slides.say: The rate is per minute, so the time must be in minutes too. Two hours is a hundred twenty minutes.
at: Two hours is a hundred twenty minutes

slides.say: Four times a hundred twenty is four hundred eighty parts.
A lot of students write four times two, eight. That mixes minutes with hours. So we always match the units first.
at: A lot of students write four times two

slides.say: Now let's see how the three quantities move together. This helps a lot in the questions.
First, when the time is fixed, the rate and the work move the same way.
A painter paints three walls an hour, for five hours. Three times five is fifteen walls.
Now she paints twice as fast, six walls an hour, in the same five hours. Six times five is thirty walls.
So twice the rate gives twice the work. That's called direct. The two go up together, by the same factor.
at: So twice the rate gives twice the work

slides.say: Second, when the rate is fixed, the time and the work also move the same way.
The same painter, three walls an hour. In four hours, three times four is twelve walls.
at: In four hours, three times four

slides.say: In two hours, that's half the time, three times two is six walls. That's half the work.
So half the time gives half the work. That's direct too.
at: So half the time gives half the work

slides.say: Third, when the work is fixed, the rate and the time move opposite ways. This is where students slip.
She has twelve walls to paint. At three walls an hour, twelve divided by three is four hours.
At six walls an hour, twice as fast, twelve divided by six is two hours. That's half the time.
So twice the rate gives half the time. The same job, done faster, takes less time. That's called inverse.
at: So twice the rate gives half the time

slides.say: Why opposite? Because the rate times the time must stay twelve. Three times four is twelve. And six times two is twelve too.
So three times as fast takes a third of the time. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
